description.narrative: (Uganda): The Biodiversity for Resilience Activity will strengthen engagement in biodiversity protection among private sector actors, protected area managers, communities, and civil society. It will promote sustainable conservation and build resilient ecosystems around priority protected areas, including lakes, national parks, and forest reserves.With FY 2022 funds, the Activity will improve the governance and management of community conservancy areas, and develop conservation enterprises, including nature-based tourism. FY 2022 funds will be used to support protection of Budongo and Kalinzu Central Forest Reserves, which are important habitats for chimpanzees. These efforts will improve the management of protected areas and buffer zones, increase conservation-based economic growth, reduce poaching and retaliatory killing of wildlife and trade in wildlife products, and support the development and implementation of the regulations and guidelines required by the 2019 Wildlife Act. These efforts will also create investment opportunities for U.S. firms, advance American national security interests, and position Uganda as a destination for sustainable tourism.The activity will contribute to GEEA Fund Priority 3: securing women's economic future through green jobs and building resilience to climate change, through promoting conservation enterprises that provide income opportunities and support women to diversify their livelihoods. The activity will address climate risks and impacts by supporting climate-smart, organic and/or restorative agriculture practices in the buffer zones....
